iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra are set to be unveiled next month with the all-new A20 Pro chip; this past weekend, a reputable tipster shared the expected performance gains based on supply chain information.

A20 Pro Chip Performance May Jump 18% with 30% Better Power Efficiency

Apple is expected to unveil its latest chip achievement—the A20 Pro—at its major September event.

The A20 Pro will be Apple's first chip manufactured using TSMC's 2nm process. It is also rumored to adopt the new Wafer-Level Multi-Chip Module (WMCM) packaging technology.

Thanks to these innovations, the market has long expected this year's chip performance gains to be more significant than in previous years.

Weibo tipster "Fixed Focus Digital" posted this weekend stating that, according to supply chain sources, the A20 Pro will deliver the following improvements over the A19 Pro:

  • 18% performance improvement
  • 30% improvement in power efficiency

When Apple officially announces the details next month, the specifics will undoubtedly be more precise. Apple typically breaks down the individual gains for the CPU, GPU, and Neural Engine separately.

However, if these figures prove accurate, they would represent a considerable leap forward. The improved power efficiency will deliver longer battery life, while performance will also reach the best level ever achieved.

Combined with iOS 27's own speed improvements, the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra are shaping up to be a highly anticipated upgrade in terms of performance.

What are your thoughts on the rumored performance gains for the A20 Pro? Let us know in the comments.
